issues.t: Takata airbag inflator recall
issues.sym: Usually nothing at all until a crash. Some owners also notice an airbag warning light.
issues.why: Older Takata airbag inflators can break down after years of heat and humidity and may burst during deployment, throwing metal pieces into the cabin. Mazda has urged owners of unrepaired older cars not to drive them.
issues.next: Look up your VIN at Mazda or NHTSA today. If an airbag recall is open, ask the dealer about towing the car in for the free repair rather than driving it.

issues.t: Rusted front crossmember (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or banging from the front end over bumps, or heavy rust visible under the front of the car.
issues.why: In states that use road salt, the front subframe can rust badly enough to weaken it. Mazda ran recalls to inspect, treat or replace it.
issues.next: Check for open recalls by VIN and have the front subframe inspected, especially if the car has spent winters in the salt belt. Do not ignore new clunks from the front.

issues.t: Dashboard top turns soft and sticky
issues.sym: The dash surface becomes tacky, shiny or soft on hot days and reflects glare onto the windshield.
issues.why: The dash material can degrade in heat and humidity, most often on cars from around 2010. A Mazda coverage extension existed but has since ended.
issues.next: Use a sunshade and a dash cover to cut glare. Replacement of the dash pad is the permanent fix.

issues.t: Spider webs block fuel tank vent (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, a fuel smell, or trouble refueling.
issues.why: Yellow sac spiders can build webs inside the evaporative vent line. The blockage creates vacuum in the tank that can crack it over time. Mazda recalled cars to update software and replace damaged tanks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Any raw fuel smell should be inspected promptly because of fire risk.

issues.t: Rear parking brake sticks from corrosion (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake drags, will not fully release, or the car feels like it is being held back after you release it.
issues.why: Water can get into the rear brake calipers and rust the parking brake mechanism inside. Mazda recalled cars to inspect and replace corroded parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If a rear wheel feels hot after driving or the car drags, have the rear brakes looked at soon.

issues.t: Engine may stall while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while you are driving or idling, often with warning lights on the dash.
issues.why: A software error in the engine computer could make it stall. Mazda reprogrammed affected cars under a recall shared with some Mazda3 and CX-5 models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free reprogramming. Stalling at speed is a safety risk.

issues.t: Fuel pump in the tank can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, hesitation, the engine stalling while driving, or cranking without starting.
issues.why: A part inside the low-pressure fuel pump can crack and stop the pump from sending fuel to the engine. Mazda recalled affected cars to replace the pump.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the pump replaced. If the engine stumbles or stalls, stop driving and have the car towed in.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning may miss a slow leak in all four tires (recall)
issues.sym: No low tire pressure light even though all four tires have slowly lost air.
issues.why: The tire pressure monitoring software may not notice when all four tires lose pressure gradually at the same rate. Mazda recalled the cars for a software fix.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Until it is done, check tire pressures with a gauge once a month.

issues.t: Door latch screws can work loose (recall)
issues.sym: A door that rattles, is hard to latch, or does not feel fully closed.
issues.why: The screws holding the door latches can back out over time. Mazda recalled the cars so dealers could apply thread-locking compound and retighten them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it done soon. If a door will not latch firmly, do not carry passengers on that side until it is fixed.

issues.t: Thermostat sticks open (code P0126)
issues.sym: Check engine light, the engine taking a long time to warm up, a temperature gauge that wanders, weak heat, or a low coolant level.
issues.why: The thermostat can stick open so the engine runs too cool. Mazda issued a series of service bulletins covering this code.
issues.next: Have the code read and the coolant level checked. Ask a Mazda dealer about bulletin 01-011/21 and its later updates.

issues.t: Cylinder deactivation fault (code P3400)
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P3400, sometimes with rough running.
issues.why: Small bits of plastic debris can plug the oil control valve that operates the cylinder deactivation system, according to a Mazda service alert.
issues.next: Have the code read soon and ask a Mazda dealer about service alert SA-047/21. Do not keep driving with a flashing check engine light.

issues.t: Fuel sender unit can leak at the top of the tank (recall)
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell, especially with a full tank, and sometimes damp fuel staining under the car near the tank.
issues.why: The sender unit on top of the fuel tank may not have been installed correctly at the factory, so fuel can seep past it.
issues.next: Stop driving it until a dealer checks the VIN and repairs it, because leaking fuel near a hot exhaust is a fire risk.

issues.t: Fog light socket can drop into the bumper (recall)
issues.sym: A fog light stops working, rattles behind the bumper, or in rare cases the bumper is scorched where the hot bulb rests against it.
issues.why: The socket holder can separate from the fog light housing and let the lit bulb fall inside the bumper cover.
issues.next: Have the dealer fit the retaining spring under the recall; until then leave the fog lights switched off.

issues.t: Brake fluid warning light may not come on (recall)
issues.sym: No warning light even when the brake fluid is low, so a leak can go unnoticed until the pedal feels soft or sinks.
issues.why: The float in the brake fluid reservoir sensor can slip off its guide, so it no longer signals a low level.
issues.next: Check the fluid level in the reservoir yourself and ask the dealer about the recall repair; a brake fluid leak needs attention immediately.

issues.t: Rear seat belt retractor may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can feel day to day; a rear belt may simply fail to lock up in a sudden stop or a crash.
issues.why: Some rear belt retractors left the factory without their retaining pins, so the locking mechanism may not hold.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN and replace the affected retractors; treat any rear belt that pulls out freely under a hard tug as unsafe.

issues.t: Fuel tank coating damage can lead to rust and leaks (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell under the car or wet staining on the tank, usually after years of road salt and moisture.
issues.why: The protective coating on California specification tanks can be damaged, which lets the steel underneath corrode and eventually weep fuel.
issues.next: Have the tank inspected under the recall and repaired or replaced; a rusting fuel tank is a fire risk and should not wait.

issues.t: Alternator belt can slip in heavy rain and trigger a charging warning (recall)
issues.sym: In a downpour or through deep water the charging warning appears and the car may go into a reduced power mode.
issues.why: Water on the accessory belt makes it slip, and the engine computer reads the dip in output as a charging failure.
issues.next: Get the free software reprogramming at a dealer; if it happens before then, pull over somewhere safe and restart the car.

issues.t: Overfilling the tank can push fuel into the charcoal canister (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell after topping off at the pump, sometimes with a rough start or a check engine light.
issues.why: Without a shut-off valve the tank can be filled past its design level, so liquid fuel reaches the charcoal vapor canister.
issues.next: Have the recall adapter and canister inspection done, and in the meantime stop filling at the first click of the pump.

issues.t: Weld debris can damage passenger seat airbag wiring (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light, a passenger airbag off light with an adult in the seat, and in some cases heavy steering from lost power assist.
issues.why: Metal debris left from welding can chafe the wiring for the passenger seat occupant sensor and short it out.
issues.next: Have the dealer fit the protective pad under the recall; until it is done treat the front passenger airbag as not working.

issues.t: Turn signals may not switch off on their own (recall)
issues.sym: After a turn the signal keeps flashing instead of cancelling, so other drivers cannot tell what you plan to do.
issues.why: Some cars with fog lights were built with the wrong combination switch behind the steering wheel.
issues.next: Have the switch replaced under the recall, and until then cancel the signal by hand after every turn.

issues.t: Navigation card makes the screen restart in cold weather
issues.sym: On cold mornings the infotainment screen reboots itself over and over, and it stops if the navigation card is pulled out.
issues.why: A batch of navigation memory cards misbehaves at low temperature and crashes the system.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the card against the bulletin and replace it; nothing else in the car is harmed by this.
